atoms.text: The ancient Olympic Games weren’t exactly the same as they are today! In ancient Greece, they were an important religious festival and had very different rules from today.
This is a list of rules for who was allowed to compete in the ancient Olympics.
atoms.sound: This is a list of rules for who was allowed to compete in the ancient Olympics. To compete, you must be: male, Greek, and a free man.

instruction.text: Could this person have competed in the ancient Olympics?

feedback.end: Women were not allowed to compete, nor were they even allowed to watch! The exception to this was the Priestess of Demeter, who was given a special seat.

instruction.text: This is a drawing of an athlete at the ancient Olympics. What is he wearing?

feedback.end: All the athletes competed while fully naked! They wanted to show off their strong bodies to Zeus and to be seen like the heroes in myths, who were usually nude in artworks.

atoms.b: Wars between different city states were very common in ancient ((++Greece France)).
The Olympic Truce was an agreement to protect all the ((++athletes mice)) and spectators.
People travelling to and from ((++Olympia Oldham)) were allowed to pass safely — even when going through lands that were at war!

instruction.text: There was another important thing that happened at the ancient Olympics. Put the word together.

feedback.end: A sacrifice is an offering to the gods, which was a common practice for the ancient Greeks. On the middle day of the Olympics, they would sacrifice 100 cows for the gods and have a big feast.

instruction.text: Winners of the ancient Olympics would be awarded with a crown made of an olive branch. Drag the crown onto the winner’s head.

feedback.end: Along with receiving the olive-branch crown, the winner would also win glory and fame. They would be welcomed home as a hero and had the right to have statues of themselves put up.
